interactions.label: Adrenarche and gonadarche are both initiated by the same increase in pulsatile G

params.question: Adrenarche and gonadarche are both initiated by the same increase in pulsatile GnRH from KNDy neurons in the arcuate nucleus.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Although gonadarche IS driven by KNDy neuron GnRH pulsatility, adrenarche is a separate process driven by adrenal androgen secretion — it is independent of the HPO axis and typically occurs about two years before gonadarche.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Adrenarche is driven by adrenal androgens (DHEA, DHEA-S) independently of the HPO axis, while gonadarche results from KNDy neuron-driven GnRH pulsatility activating LH and FSH release. Adrenarche typically occurs about two years before gonadarche.

interactions.label: A six-year-old girl presents with breast development and accelerated growth. Her

params.question: A six-year-old girl presents with breast development and accelerated growth. Her serum LH is elevated and rises further after GnRH stimulation. What does this hormonal pattern indicate?

answers.text: Peripheral precocious puberty caused by an autonomous source of oestrogen

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. In peripheral precocious puberty, the source of sex steroids is independent of the HPO axis, so LH and FSH are typically suppressed and do NOT respond to GnRH stimulation.

answers.text: A benign variant such as premature thelarche, requiring only observation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Premature thelarche presents with isolated breast budding, normal growth velocity, and prepubertal gonadotrophin levels — not the elevated, GnRH-responsive LH seen here.

answers.text: Central precocious puberty due to premature activation of the HPO axis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Elevated LH that rises further on GnRH stimulation confirms that the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis has been prematurely activated — the hallmark of central (gonadotrophin-dependent) precocious puberty.

answers.text: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia with excess adrenal androgen production

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia produces excess adrenal androgens, not pituitary gonadotrophins. LH would not be elevated or GnRH-responsive in that condition.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the key rule: in central precocious puberty, LH is elevated and GnRH-responsive because the HPO axis itself is active. In peripheral precocious puberty, LH is suppressed because the sex steroid source is independent of the axis.
Excellent. The GnRH stimulation test is the pivotal investigation that separates central from peripheral precocious puberty, and this distinction determines the entire treatment approach.

interactions.label: A 14-year-old girl has Tanner stage B3 breasts but has not yet had menarche. She

params.question: A 14-year-old girl has Tanner stage B3 breasts but has not yet had menarche. She is short for her age, has a webbed neck, and a wide carrying angle at the elbows. Which diagnosis do these examination findings most strongly suggest?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Constitutional delay is the commonest cause of delayed puberty, but it presents with an otherwise normal examination and a family history of late puberty — not with dysmorphic features such as a webbed neck or wide carrying angle.
Incorrect. Kallmann syndrome presents with delayed puberty and anosmia (loss of smell) due to defective GnRH neuron migration, not with the somatic features described here.
Incorrect. Imperforate hymen presents with cyclical abdominal pain and a bulging membrane on examination, typically in a girl who has normal pubertal development but no visible menstrual flow.

Correct. Short stature combined with a webbed neck, wide carrying angle (cubitus valgus), and delayed puberty is the classic presentation of Turner syndrome. These somatic features should prompt karyotype analysis.

overallFeedback.feedback: The combination of short stature, webbed neck, and wide carrying angle (cubitus valgus) alongside delayed puberty is classic for Turner syndrome (45,X). Each differential — constitutional delay, Kallmann, obstruction — has its own signature findings.

Well done. Recognising the somatic features of Turner syndrome during examination is essential, as it requires lifelong multidisciplinary care including oestrogen replacement, growth hormone therapy, and cardiac surveillance.

interactions.label: A seven-year-old girl has isolated breast budding without pubic hair, normal gro

params.question: A seven-year-old girl has isolated breast budding without pubic hair, normal growth velocity, and no other pubertal changes over six months of follow-up. Which feature most strongly suggests this is a benign variant rather than true precocious puberty?

answers.text: Her age is above six years, making precocious puberty unlikely

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The threshold for precocious puberty in girls is eight years, not six. Breast development before age eight warrants evaluation regardless of whether the child is six or seven.

answers.text: Breast tissue alone, without progression, confirms central precocious puberty

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect — the opposite is true. Isolated breast budding without progression is the hallmark of premature thelarche, a benign variant, not central precocious puberty.

answers.text: The absence of progressive, coordinated pubertal development across multiple signs

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. True precocious puberty shows coordinated progression — breast enlargement, pubic hair, growth acceleration, and eventually menarche advance together. An isolated finding that does not progress over months points to a benign variant such as premature thelarche.

answers.text: Normal growth velocity rules out any form of precocious puberty

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While accelerated growth velocity is common in true precocious puberty, normal velocity alone does not completely exclude it. Here, it is the combined picture — isolated finding plus absence of progression — that favours a benign variant.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key distinction is progression: true precocious puberty shows coordinated advancement of multiple pubertal signs, while benign variants such as premature thelarche present with a single, non-progressive finding.
Excellent. Distinguishing benign variants from true precocious puberty avoids unnecessary treatment — benign variants need only monitoring and reassurance, not GnRH analogues.

interactions.label: A girl with confirmed central precocious puberty is started on a GnRH analogue.

params.question: A girl with confirmed central precocious puberty is started on a GnRH analogue. By which mechanism does this treatment suppress pubertal progression?

answers.text: It blocks oestrogen receptors in the breast and uterus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Blocking oestrogen receptors is the mechanism of anti-oestrogens such as tamoxifen. GnRH analogues act at the pituitary level, not at target tissues.

answers.text: It provides continuous GnRH, which downregulates pituitary GnRH receptors and stops LH/FSH release

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. GnRH analogues deliver continuous GnRH instead of the normal pulsatile pattern. This continuous stimulation desensitises the pituitary GnRH receptors, shutting down LH and FSH secretion and halting pubertal progression.

answers.text: It directly inhibits the KNDy neurons in the arcuate nucleus

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. GnRH analogues do not act at the hypothalamic KNDy neuron level. They act at the pituitary, where continuous receptor stimulation causes receptor downregulation.

answers.text: It enhances adrenal androgen metabolism, reducing peripheral sex steroid levels

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. GnRH analogues have no direct effect on adrenal androgen production or metabolism. They specifically target the pituitary gonadotrophin axis.

overallFeedback.feedback: GnRH analogues work by converting the normal pulsatile GnRH signal into a continuous one. This paradoxically desensitises the pituitary receptors, stopping LH and FSH release and halting pubertal progression until treatment is withdrawn.

Well done. This mechanism also explains why GnRH analogues work only in central precocious puberty — in peripheral cases, sex steroids come from sources independent of the pituitary, so suppressing LH and FSH has no effect.
